chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When a man divorces his wife before consummating the marriage, there is no waiting period upon her; she may marry from that very moment if she wishes, and one divorce makes her irrevocably divorced; and if he had stipulated a dower for her, she is entitled to half of what he stipulated.
ai.seo_question: What are the rights of a wife divorced before consummation in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Reported by Shaykh al-Kulayni in al-Kafi, this hadith clarifies the fiqh of khulu' or talaq before consummation, establishing that the absence of sexual intercourse negates the obligation of the three-month waiting period (iddah), allowing for immediate remarriage. It further codifies the financial right of the wife to half the stipulated mahr, reflecting the principle of compensation for the sanctity of the marriage contract even without physical union. This ruling is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing between the legal effects of the contract versus the act of consummation.
